question: Does simple low-loss connectivity between neural-network solutions reveal whether they use the same predictive mechanisms, and can deliberately breaking linear connectivity remove reliance on a spurious cue?

key_findings.claim: The paper operationalizes mechanistic similarity as equality of the sets of data-generating-process interventions to which two models are invariant.
key_findings.evidence: A latent-variable generator and unit interventions define counterfactual datasets; models are called mechanistically similar when the same interventions leave their loss unchanged.

key_findings.claim: Mechanistically dissimilar synthetic-image classifiers can be joined by learned quadratic low-loss paths even when direct linear interpolation remains obstructed after neuron permutation.
key_findings.evidence: Across ResNet-18 and VGG-13 models trained with versus without box, color, or Dominoes cues, quadratic paths fit on a chosen dataset avoid its barrier, while the linear and activation-matched linear paths show barriers and different counterfactual behavior.

key_findings.claim: Naive fine-tuning often preserves the pretrained shortcut at small or medium learning rates, whereas a large update can cross a linear barrier and change counterfactual behavior.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 varies cue prevalence and learning rate for VGG-13 and ResNet-18; low-barrier interpolations accompany similar cue responses, while large-learning-rate endpoints show barriers and stronger cue invariance.

key_findings.claim: Connectivity-Based Fine-Tuning combines a deliberately induced interpolation barrier with class-mean representation matching on 2,500 clean examples.
key_findings.evidence: CBFT alternates a capped barrier objective on random points between the candidate and original model with an invariance penalty between class-average representations from cue-bearing and clean data.

key_findings.claim: CBFT improves cue removal in many cells but the paper's claim of complete invariance is contradicted by its own hardest table entries.
key_findings.evidence: Direct inspection of Table 1 shows strong CIFAR-10 behavior, e.g. at 60% cue prevalence NC/C/RC/RI accuracies 74.1/71.5/73.4/8.75. On CIFAR-100, however, the corresponding values are 42.7/65.0/36.4/14.6, and at 90% they are 28.5/72.9/23.2/46.0, far from cue invariance and sometimes poor on randomized images.

key_findings.claim: The formal appendix does not prove the headline conjecture in its stated direction.
key_findings.evidence: Conjecture 1 is lack of linear connectivity implies mechanistic dissimilarity. Theorem 1 instead establishes, in a one-hidden-layer construction and only for mechanisms of different complexity, mechanistic dissimilarity implies lack of linear connectivity; the same-complexity case is then dismissed with a plausibility argument rather than a theorem.

key_findings.claim: Additional definition-to-proof gaps weaken the proposed mechanistic diagnostic.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 3 equates invariance with equality of expected loss, but Proposition 1's proof substitutes pointwise equality of model outputs. Corollary 1 further treats small Wasserstein distance between marginal activation rates as implying a usable global neuron permutation, which is not sufficient to align per-input activation patterns or outputs.

method.core_idea: Use counterfactual invariances to give mode connectivity a behavioral interpretation, then optimize away from the original model's linear basin while matching representations across clean and shortcut-bearing data.
method.mechanism: Synthetic label-correlated cues create models with known shortcut dependence; counterfactual cue and image interventions probe mechanisms; linear, permutation-aligned linear, and learned quadratic paths test connectivity; CBFT jointly fits clean labels, raises loss at random interpolation points, and aligns class-average representations.
assumptions: Inputs have an invertible generative map with independent, manipulable latent factors.
Equality of loss under selected interventions faithfully identifies the attributes used by a model.
The finite intervention set exhausts task-relevant mechanisms.
Activation matching adequately accounts for relevant architectural symmetries.
Synthetic low-complexity cues stand in for realistic spurious correlations.
A linear barrier is causally informative about mechanism change rather than merely parameter alignment or optimization history.
Matching class means is sufficient to induce the desired invariance while preserving useful features.

techniques.role: Defines and measures mechanistic similarity through controlled changes to latent attributes.
Creates box-location, box-color, and concatenated-image shortcuts with known counterfactuals.
Tests for a loss barrier on direct weight interpolation.
Greedily permutes neurons before testing linear interpolation.
Learns a one-bend path whose middle parameters minimize loss on a selected dataset.
Combines clean-data classification, barrier induction, and representation invariance objectives.

evaluations.setting: ResNet-18 and VGG-13 trained on CIFAR-10 with versus without a label-located 3x3 box cue.
evaluations.metric: Train/test accuracy and loss along quadratic, linear, and permutation-aligned linear paths on four counterfactual datasets.
evaluations.result: Quadratic paths connect endpoints on their fitting distribution; linear paths retain barriers and endpoints respond differently to cue or image randomization.
evaluations.baseline: Direct linear interpolation and Git Re-Basin-style activation matching.

evaluations.setting: Pretraining on partially or perfectly cue-correlated CIFAR-10 followed by 100-epoch clean-data fine-tuning.
evaluations.metric: Counterfactual accuracy along the pretrained-to-fine-tuned linear path.
evaluations.result: Small and medium learning rates often preserve linear connectivity and shortcut behavior; large learning rates more often produce a barrier and cue-invariant endpoint.
evaluations.baseline: Naive fine-tuning across three initial learning rates.

evaluations.setting: ResNet-18 on synthetic CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Dominoes with 60%-90% cue prevalence and 2,500 clean samples.
evaluations.metric: Mean of three-seed accuracies on no-cue, cue, randomized-cue, and randomized-image test sets.
evaluations.result: CBFT usually reduces shortcut reliance more than the listed baselines, but sacrifices clean accuracy and fails approximate invariance badly in several CIFAR-100 cells.
evaluations.baseline: Small/medium naive fine-tuning, last-layer retraining, and linear-probe then fine-tune.

evaluations.setting: CBFT objective ablations on all three synthetic datasets.
evaluations.result: Removing the barrier term generally preserves cue reliance; removing class-mean invariance can induce anti-correlation, so both terms contribute distinct effects.
evaluations.baseline: CBFT without the barrier loss or without the invariance loss.

evaluations.setting: One-hidden-layer ReLU network on 50,000 synthetic 128-dimensional examples with K=0 and K=4 predictive attributes.
evaluations.metric: Loss differences under intervention, activation-rate Wasserstein distance, and interpolation loss.
evaluations.result: Models using the constructed different-complexity attributes show large activation-rate distance and barriers; same-mechanism pairs can be aligned.
evaluations.baseline: Pairs trained with either or both synthetic attributes.

limitations: Author-stated: the central lack-of-linear-connectivity claim is a conjecture outside a simplified one-hidden-layer setting.
Author-stated: quadratic paths are fitted to a dataset and need not retain low loss on counterfactual distributions.
Author-stated: large-learning-rate fine-tuning can destroy pretrained features and lose sample efficiency.
Reviewer inference: all robustness experiments use conspicuous synthetic cues rather than natural spurious-correlation benchmarks.
Reviewer inference: only three-seed means are reported, without dispersion or significance tests.
Reviewer inference: CBFT requires the original cue-bearing data, a clean labeled subset, and advance knowledge of the attribute to suppress.
Reviewer inference: class-mean matching does not imply distributional or per-example invariance.
Reviewer inference: Table 1 mixes desired directions across four metrics and shows large residual cue dependence, especially on CIFAR-100.
Reviewer inference: the formal result reverses the direction of the headline conjecture and relies on unusually strong interpolation, simplicity-bias, and generative assumptions.
failure_modes: A linear barrier arises from neuron misalignment, scale symmetry, batch-normalization state, or optimization history rather than a different prediction rule.
Two models use different mechanisms of comparable complexity yet remain linearly connected, defeating the diagnostic.
Two models share a mechanism but a greedy permutation fails, producing a false barrier.
Expected loss remains unchanged under an intervention even though predictions change on compensating subsets.
Class-average representations match while within-class shortcut information remains decodable.
The barrier objective is satisfied by anti-correlating with the cue or damaging useful features rather than learning the desired mechanism.
CBFT reduces cue sensitivity but lowers no-cue accuracy enough to be operationally worse.
The relevant real-world nuisance cannot be isolated or counterfactually manipulated, so mechanistic similarity is unidentifiable.
reusable_insights: Weight-space connectivity should be evaluated jointly with behavior on deliberately shifted or counterfactual data; source-distribution loss alone hides mechanism changes.
A learned connectivity path is conditional on the data used to fit it and should be tested on held-out environments.
Post-hoc robustness claims need a scalar selection criterion plus clean, worst-group, and intervention metrics with uncertainty.
When using an optimization proxy for mechanism change, directly probe whether the unwanted feature remains decodable instead of inferring success from the proxy.
The direction of every implication in a mechanistic theorem matters: evidence for dissimilarity causing barriers does not establish that every barrier diagnoses dissimilarity.
open_questions: Does lack of linear connectivity predict mechanism change after exhaustive symmetry handling on natural-image, language, and foundation-model tasks?
Can mechanistic similarity be defined without an invertible known generator or exact counterfactuals?
What additional conditions would make the headline lack-of-connectivity implication provable in its stated direction?
Does CBFT outperform last-layer and group-robust methods on Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, and WILDS under equal tuning and data budgets?
Can distributional alignment or explicit feature-unlearning replace class-mean matching and prevent residual decodability?
How much useful pretrained capability is lost as a function of the induced barrier height?

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Connectivity Reveals Generalization Strategies
competitive_landscape.difference: Juneja et al. independently find linear-connectivity clusters aligned with distinct NLP heuristics on diagnostic datasets. It supplies natural-language corroboration but not the reviewed paper's intervention definition or CBFT method.

competitive_landscape.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
competitive_landscape.difference: Ainsworth et al. introduce activation and weight matching to recover linear connectivity after neuron permutation; the reviewed work uses activation matching, then interprets residual barriers behaviorally rather than as a model-merging failure alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Last Layer Re-Training is Sufficient for Robustness to Spurious Correlations
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep Feature Reweighting changes only the classifier on balanced data and reports natural spurious-correlation benchmarks; CBFT changes the full model to alter mechanisms, with more expressive intervention but materially stronger data and optimization requirements.

competitive_landscape.title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
competitive_landscape.difference: Kumar et al. motivate linear-probe then fine-tune to preserve useful features across ten natural distribution shifts. CBFT instead seeks deliberate disconnection from the pretrained solution to remove a known shortcut, increasing the risk of feature damage.

competitive_landscape.title: A Closer Look at Model Adaptation using Feature Distortion and Simplicity Bias
competitive_landscape.difference: This work studies adaptation protocols through feature distortion and simplicity bias on OOD behavior, offering a more direct feature-space account of failure than CBFT's use of an interpolation barrier as a mechanism proxy.

competitive_landscape.title: Not Only the Last-Layer Features for Spurious Correlations: All Layer Deep Feature Reweighting
competitive_landscape.difference: All-Layer DFR selects less biased features throughout the network and targets worst-group accuracy on standard benchmarks. It directly addresses the possibility that desired features disappear by the last layer, while CBFT seeks a different basin without testing feature decodability layer by layer.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Mechanistic similarity can be formalized through shared counterfactual invariances; lack of linear connectivity diagnoses dissimilar mechanisms and enables targeted, sample-efficient mechanism editing through CBFT.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper links synthetic interventions, several path families, VGG/ResNet experiments, a simplified ReLU analysis, and a two-term fine-tuning objective with extensive appendix plots and ablations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The behavioral lens on mode connectivity and barrier-based editing objective are original and useful hypotheses. The strongest diagnostic claim remains a conjecture, its advertised proof runs in the opposite direction, and Table 1 does not support complete invariance; the contribution is best treated as a synthetic empirical program rather than an established mechanistic test.

reviewer_notes: Read the full 40-page ICML/arXiv artifact and directly rendered and inspected PDF Figures 4-6 and 13 plus Tables 1, 3-5 because the cached extraction carried rotated-layout risk. The collection's editorial title prefix was excluded; the stable OpenReview identity was retained. Competitors were checked at primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
